'''Stefano Mancuso''' (born 9 May 1965) is an Italian [[botanist]] and writer, best known for his research on [[plant intelligence]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Volkenburgh, Elizabeth Van|year=2016|title=Review of Brilliant Green: The Surprising History and Science of Plant Intelligence|journal=The Quarterly Review of Biology|volume=91|issue=1|pages=100–101|doi=10.1086/685354|jstor=26553466}}</ref> He is professor of the Agriculture, Food, Environment and Forestry department at his alma mater, the [[University of Florence]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Stefano Mancuso's current academic rank and department information | publisher = The University Of Florence official website | url =https://www.unifi.it/p-doc2-2020-200001-M-3f2a3d31342a2f-0.html| access-date = 3 October 2020}}</ref> He  is the director of the International Laboratory of Plant Neurobiology,<ref>{{cite web | title = Membership list of the LINV project | publisher = The International Laboratory of Plant Neurobiology official website | url =http://www.linv.org/people| access-date = 3 October 2020}}</ref> steering committee member of the [[Society of Plant Signaling and Behavior]],<ref>{{cite web | title = The Society of Plant Signaling and Behavior steering committee list| publisher = The Society of Plant Signaling and Behavior official website | url=https://www.plantbehavior.org/who-we-are | access-date = 3 October 2020}}</ref> editor-in-chief of the ''Plant Signaling & Behavior'' journal<ref>{{cite web|title=Editorial board list of the Plant Signaling & Behavior journal|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=editorialBoard&journalCode=kpsb20|website=Taylor & Francis Group website|access-date=3 October 2020}}</ref> and a member of the [[Accademia dei Georgofili]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Academic list 2019 | publisher=The Accademia dei Georgofili official website|url =http://www.georgofili.it/Media?c=2778dd64-8300-4404-a1fd-5c825a41140d|access-date=3 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Il georgofilo Stefano Mancuso è uno dei "20 italiani che ci cambieranno la vita" |publisher=Information newsletter by the Accademia dei Georgofili|url =http://www.georgofili.info/contenuti/il-georgofilo-stefano-mancuso--uno-dei-20-italiani-che-ci-cambieranno-la-vita/936|access-date=3 October 2020}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Mancuso developed an interest in the research of plants during his university studies.<ref name="franceculture.fr">{{Cite web|url=https://www.franceculture.fr/emissions/les-matins-du-samedi/stefano-mancuso-denis-pelletier | title = Stefano Mancuso's interview on the french radio| date = 20 April 2019|publisher=France Culture radio (20 April 2019)|language=fr|access-date=5 October 2020}}</ref> Since 2001, he has been a professor at the University of Florence, and in 2005 he founded the International Laboratory of Plant Neurobiology, designed to study physiology, behavior, molecular biology, intelligence, and other fields of plant science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.linv.org/about-us/|title=LINV AT FIRST GLANCE | publisher = The International Laboratory for Plant Neurobiology official website | access-date = 5 October 2020}}</ref>

== Research ==
=== Root system of plants ===
Mancuso studied the abilities of plants and their [[Root|root system]] (in particular, the tips of the roots, which are very sensitive to various types of stimuli,<ref>Baluska F., Mancuso S., Volkmann D., & Barlow, P. W. (2010) ''Root apex transition zone: a signalling-response nexus in the root''. Trends in plant science, 15(7), 402—408.</ref> such as pressure, temperature, certain sounds, humidity, and damage).<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.3389/fpls.2013.00354 | doi-access=free | title=Root Apex Transition Zone as Oscillatory Zone | date=2013 | last1=Baluška | first1=František | last2=Mancuso | first2=Stefano | journal=Frontiers in Plant Science | volume=4 | page=354 | pmid=24106493 | pmc=3788588 }}</ref> According to an article published in 2004 by a group of botanists (which included Mancuso), the areas of the root apices interact with each other, forming a structure whose functions they proposed to be similar to the functions of an animal's brain.<ref name="ApexFx2004">Baluska F., Mancuso S., Volkmann D., & Barlow P. (2004) ''[http://www.esalq.usp.br/lepse/imgs/paginas_thumb/mini/Root-apices-as-plant-command-centres---brain-like--status-of-the-root-apex-transition-zone.pdf Root apices as plant command centres: the unique ‘brain-like’ status of the root apex transition zone]''. Biologia, 59(Suppl 13), 7-19.</ref>

=== Plant perception ===
{{Further|Plant perception (physiology)|label1=Plant perception}}
Mancuso concluded that in the course of evolution, plants had to work out solutions to the problems inherent in organisms attached to a substrate. Although plants have neither nerves nor a brain, they have a social life and, therefore, analogues of the sensory organs, though very different from those in animals. He considers the key to understanding this can be found in some cells (gametes and bacteria), corals, sponges, and in the behaviour of organisms such as [[placozoa]]. In 2012, Mancuso and his colleagues found that plants have receptors that make their roots sensitive to sound and the direction of its distribution.<ref>Gagliano M., Mancuso S. & Robert D. (2012) ''Towards understanding plant bioacoustics''. Trends in plant science, 17(6), 323—325.</ref> Other biologists four years prior claimed that trees in conditions of acute water shortage can emit sounds which can be more than just passive signs of [[cavitation]].<ref>Zweifel R. & Zeugin F. (2008) ''Ultrasonic acoustic emissions in drought-stressed trees — more than signals from cavitation?'' New Phytol. 179, 1070—1079</ref>

[[Phytoplankton]] and terrestrial plants have certain abilities for the perception of light. Mancuso and his colleagues showed that in the laboratory [[arabidopsis]] the root apices are very sensitive to light (a few seconds of illumination are enough to cause an immediate and strong reaction of the molecules of the [[Reactive oxygen species|ROS]]). These phenomena complemented earlier observations and studies of living roots made using [[confocal microscopy]].<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.4161/psb.6.10.18165 | title=Illumination of Arabidopsis roots induces immediate burst of ROS production | date=2011 | last1=Yokawa | first1=Ken | last2=Kagenishi | first2=Tomoko | last3=Kawano | first3=Tomonori | last4=Mancuso | first4=Stefano | last5=Baluška | first5=František | journal=Plant Signaling & Behavior | volume=6 | issue=10 | pages=1460–1464 | pmid=21957498 | pmc=3256371 | bibcode=2011PlSiB...6.1460Y }}</ref>

His book ''Plant revolution: le piante hanno già inventato il nostro futuro'',<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=R5UkMQAACAAJ&q=plant+revolution+stefano|title=Plant revolution: le piante hanno già inventato il nostro futuro|isbn=9788809831360|access-date=6 October 2020|last1=Mancuso|first1=Stefano|year=2017|publisher=Giunti }}</ref> describes his view of how plants have found and tested "brilliant" solutions to the various problems that humanity faces today for hundreds of millions of years. Plants, partly due to symbiosis with bacteria and fungi, "invented" well-optimized and stable methods of colonizing the earth's surface and then the lower atmosphere. Plants also created one of the most important [[carbon sink]]s on our planet, and launched the production of clean energy from [[starch]], [[sucrose]], [[sclerenchyma]] and complex [[biomolecule]]s through [[photosynthesis|photosynthetic]] [[chlorophyll]], [[biodegradability]] according to the principles of a [[circular economy]].

According to  Mancuso, since the beginning of the 1990s, some scientists began to recognize that plants have not only the ability to communicate with each other, but also their own form of intelligence.<ref>Trewavas A. (2003) ''Aspects of plant intelligence''. Annals of Botany 92:1-20</ref><ref>Trewavas A. Plant intelligence. Naturwissenschaften 2005a;92:401-13.</ref><ref>Trewavas A. Green plants as intelligent organisms. Trends Plant Sci 2005; 10:413-9.</ref><ref>Trewavas A. Response to Alpi et al.: ''Plant neurobiology — all metaphors have value''. Trends in Plant Science 2007; 12:231</ref>

=== Plants and animals ===
Mancuso notes that vascular plants have an analogue of the circulatory system, consisting of several organs (in particular reproductive organs), but that, unlike highly organized animals, plants have receptors distributed throughout the body, while animals have receptors concentrated in specific organs such as eyes, ears, skin, and tongue. The reproductive organs of plants are diverse in principle of their functioning, while in animals, they are more unified. According to Mancuso, this suggests that the plants "smell", "listen", "communicate" (between individuals of the same species, and sometimes with other species) and "learn"<ref>Volkov A.G, Carrell H., Adesina T., Markin V.S. & Jovanov E. (2008) ''Plant electrical memory''. Plant Signaling & Behavior 3:490-492</ref> (through a certain form of memory, including the memory of their immune system<ref>Baldwin I.T. & Schmelz E.A (1996) ''Immunological «memory» in the induced accumulation of nicotine in wild Tobacco''. Ecology 77:236-246</ref>), using their entire modular organism (which allows plants to resist both predatory and herbivorous animals better). Mancuso often refers to [[lima bean]] as an example, which, when attacked by [[Tetranychus urticae|red spider mite (lat. tetranychus urticae)]], releases a complex of molecules into the air that can attract ''[[phytoseiulus persimilis]]'', carnivorous mites that are ready to consume colonies of the red spider mites. Mancuso and his colleagues emphasized the role of [[auxin]]s, which function as [[neurotransmitter]]s{{citation needed|date=October 2023}}, similar to those found in animals.

Plants are able to synthesize molecules that play a role similar to animal [[neuron]]s,<ref name=ApexFx2004/> in particular [[synaptotagmin]]s and [[monosodium glutamate]].<ref name=ApexFx2004/> Plants can carry out the biosynthesis of molecules that are supposed to be homologous to molecules that perform important functions in animals (for example, molecules that activate [[immunophilins]]<ref>Bailly A., Sovero V., Vincenzetti V., Santelia D., Bartnik D., Koenig B. W., … & Geisler M. (2008). ''[http://www.jbc.org/content/283/31/21817.full.pdf Modulation of P-glycoproteins by auxin transport inhibitors is mediated by interaction with immunophilins].'' Journal of Biological Chemistry, 283(31), 21817-21826.</ref> that perform immune and hormonal functions in animals, in particular, signalling of steroid and neurological hormones). [[Cytology]] confirms the existence of plant cells behaving as synapses{{citation needed|date=October 2023}}. In 2005, Mancuso, together with several biochemists, developed a "non-invasive" microelectrode based on [[carbon nanotube]] technology for measuring and fixing the flow of information that can circulate in plants.<ref name="Mancuso2005">Mancuso S., Marras A. M., Magnus V., & Baluška F. (2005) [http://www.esalq.usp.br/lepse/imgs/conteudo_thumb/Noninvasive-and-continuous-recordings-of-auxin-fluxes-in-intact-root-apex-with-a-carbon-nanotube-modiWed-and-self-referencing-microelectrode-1.pdf Noninvasive and continuous recordings of auxin fluxes in intact root apex with a carbon nanotube-modified and self-referencing microelectrode]. Analytical biochemistry, 341(2), 344–351</ref>

=== Plant intelligence ===
{{Further|Plant intelligence}}
Mancuso notes that for a very long time, [[intelligence]] was mistakenly considered by many people to be "what distinguishes us from other living beings," but if we consider intelligence as the ability to solve and overcome problems, we have to recognize that plants possess it, and it is intelligence that allows plants to develop and respond to most of the problems that they encounter throughout their ontogenesis.<ref>{{cite journal |author = Brenner E. D., Stahlberg R., Mancuso S., Vivanco J., Baluska F., Van Volkenburgh E. |title= Plant neurobiology: an integrated view of plant signaling |journal= Trends in Plant Science|type= journal |edition= Trends in Plant Science  |year= 2006 |publisher= Cell Press |volume= 11 |number= 8|pages = 413–419 |doi = 10.1016/j.tplants.2006.06.009 |pmid = 16843034 |bibcode= 2006TPS....11..413B |language= en }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author = Trewavas, Anthony |title= Green plants as intelligent organisms |journal= Trends in Plant Science|edition= Trends in Plant Science  |year= 2005 |publisher= Cell Press |volume= 10 |number= 9|pages = 413–419 |doi = 10.1016/j.tplants.2005.07.005 |pmid = 16054860 |bibcode= 2005TPS....10..413T |ref= Trewavas |language= en }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |author = Trewavas, A. |title= Mindless mastery |journal= Nature|edition= Nature  |year= 2002 |volume= 415 |number= 6874|pages = 841 |doi = 10.1038/415841a |bibcode = 2002Natur.415..841T |pmid = 11859344 |s2cid= 4350140|language= en |doi-access= free }}</ref>

Thus, plants adapt to life in almost all sufficiently lit terrestrial and aquatic environments, encountering both herbivores and predatory insects and animals. Although plants do not have a specific organ comparable to the brain, they use the equivalent of the so-called "Diffuse brain" (it. "Cervello diffuso").<ref name="franceculture.fr"/> Some plants, for example, are capable of secreting substances that attract insects and animals that plants use for their own needs. Chemicals synthesized by plants often have a very complex effect on the behaviour of animals and insects (an example is the mutually beneficial relationship of [[myrmecophyte]]s and [[ant]]s, in particular the phenomenon of the [[devil's garden]] in Amazonian forests).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://xren.su/ants-and-symbiosis/|title = Умные муравьи. Часть 1: Симбиоз с растениями от 09.02.2018.|publisher=Hren.su|language=ru|access-date=6 October 2020}}</ref>

Mancuso has also advocated for bacterial intelligence.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Barnett, Judith B.|year=2015|title=Review of Mancuso, Stefano and Alessandra Viola. Brilliant Green: The Surprising History and Science of Plant Intelligence|journal=Library Journal|url=https://digitalcommons.uri.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1075&context=lib_ts_pubs|volume=140|issue=3|pages=126}}</ref> He has controversially argued that plants have consciousness. This idea is rejected by the majority of plant scientists as plants do not possess a brain or neurons.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Taiz, Lincoln; Alkon, Daniel; Draguhn, Andreas; Murphy, Angus; Blatt, Michael; Hawes, Chris; Thiel, Gerhard; Robinson, David G.|year=2019|title=Plants Neither Possess nor Require Consciousness|journal=Trends in Plant Science|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1360138519301268|volume=24|issue=8|pages=677–687|doi=10.1016/j.tplants.2019.05.008|pmid=31279732 |bibcode=2019TPS....24..677T |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="Mallatt 2020">{{cite journal|author=Mallatt J, Blatt MR, Draguhn A, Robinson DG, Taiz L.|year=2020|title=Debunking a myth: plant consciousness|journal= Protoplasma|volume=258|issue=3|pages=459–476| doi=10.1007/s00709-020-01579-w|pmid=33196907|pmc=8052213}}</ref>

== Professional activities ==
In 2010, Mancuso gave a lecture in Oxford on the movement of roots in the soil: how they look for water, nutrients and capture new spaces.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The interview with Stefano Mancuso by Frederic Mouchon. April 8, 2018. ''Stefano Mancuso, l'homme qui murmure a l'oreille des plantes''|date=8 April 2018 |url=http://www.leparisien.fr/societe/stefano-mancuso-l-homme-qui-murmure-a-l-oreille-des-plantes-08-04-2018-7652796.php|access-date=5 October 2020|publisher=Le Parisien|language=fr}}</ref> Mancuso was also an invited speaker at the [[TED (conference)|TED Global conference]] in the same year.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stefano Mancuso. ''The roots of plant intelligence''|date=11 October 2010 |url=https://www.ted.com/talks/stefano_mancuso_the_roots_of_plant_intelligence#t-1386|access-date=5 October 2020|publisher=www.ted.com}}</ref>

In 2012, in the [[Plantoid]] project, he took part in the creation of a "bio-inspired" robot that imitated certain natural properties of the roots, and could, for example, explore an area that is difficult to access or contaminated as a result of a nuclear accident or the use of bacteriological weapons.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The interview with Stefano Mancuso by Frederic Mouchon. April 8, 2018. ''Stefano Mancuso, l'homme qui murmure a l'oreille des plantes''|date=8 April 2018 |url=http://www.leparisien.fr/societe/stefano-mancuso-l-homme-qui-murmure-a-l-oreille-des-plantes-08-04-2018-7652796.php|access-date=5 October 2020|publisher=Le Parisien|language=fr}}</ref> The Plantoid project is still developing for the [[European Commission]] by consortium of the scientists including Mancuso.<ref>{{cite web|title = Consortium | publisher = The Plantoid project official website| url=https://www.plantoidproject.eu/index.php/the-project/partnership| access-date=2021-01-18}}</ref>

In 2013,  with co-author Alessandra Viola, he published the book ''Verde brillante: Sensibilità e intelligenza  del mondo  vegetale.'' <ref>{{Cite book|last1=Mancuso|first1=Stefano|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bJ1PDwAAQBAJ&q=L+Intelligence+des+plantes|title=L Intelligence des plantes|last2=Temperini|first2=Renaud|last3=Viola|first3=Alessandra|date=4 April 2018|publisher=Albin Michel |isbn=9782226430120|access-date=5 October 2020}}</ref>

In 2014, at the University of Florence, Mancuso created a startup specializing in plant [[Bionics|biomimetics]] and an autonomous floating greenhouse,<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Jellyfish Barge project|work=piante Innovative |date=19 October 2015 |url=https://www.pianteinnovative.it/2015/10/19/jellyfish-barge/|access-date=5 October 2020|publisher=www.pianteinnovative.it|language=it}}</ref> which was offered for mass production to the Chilean government in 2016.

In 2017, he published ''Plant revolution: le piante hanno già inventato il nostro futuro.'' The  English translation of the book, ''The Revolutionary Genius of Plants: A New Understanding of Plant Intelligence and Behavior,''  was written by Vanessa Di Stefano.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Mancuso |first1=Stefano |title=The Revolutionary Genius of Plants: A New Understanding of Plant Intelligence and Behavior |date=2017 |publisher=Atria Books |location=Copyright page |isbn=978-1-5011-8785-8}}</ref>
